description: Run by .github/workflows/renovate.yml, which lists the setup it needs.

Every commit and PR title is chore(deps), security fixes included: release-please does not release on chore, so a dependency update never cuts a release by itself. Security fixes skip the wait, the schedule, the release age and the approval: those are the vulnerabilityAlerts defaults, which Renovate applies last and packageRules cannot override. vulnerabilityAlerts repeats the commit type, which packageRules would otherwise decide for them.

Every npm dependency except the test-only serve and @playwright/test can change what ships, so each of its updates waits for a tick on the Dependency Dashboard, as does every major (security fixes excepted, majors included). vite, typescript and @playwright/test are pinned to exact versions in package.json, so the monthly lock file maintenance cannot move them; only an update of their own does.

Renovate updates direct dependencies only. Transitive ones move with the monthly lock file maintenance, except exact-pinned children such as playwright and playwright-core, which move only with their parent's update.
ignorePaths is config:recommended's list without **/test/**, so the custom manager below can read test/README.md.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Transitive dependencies have no update of their own, and OSV and GitHub alerts cannot fix them: regenerating package-lock.json within the declared ranges is what moves them. Monthly, the first Monday, since it rewrites the whole lock file. The release age still applies through npm's --before; the branch itself has no release timestamp, so the age check must not wait for one. No PR limits: it sorts after every other branch, so the limits would starve it, and with one run a week it would then miss its first-Monday window for the month.
prBodyNotes: **Can change what ships.** This regenerates every package in package-lock.json within the declared ranges. Transitive build dependencies (rollup, esbuild, postcss and others) shape the bundles; vite, typescript and Playwright are pinned exactly and do not move. Run `npm run build` and `npm run build:npm` on `main` and on this branch and diff `dist/` and `dist-npm/` before merging.
If this PR carries an artifact notice that npm was re-run without `--before`, no release age was applied to this lock file: review it accordingly.

customManagers.description: The Playwright Docker image used to regenerate the Linux baselines (package.json's test:pw:update:linux and test/README.md) must match @playwright/test. Looked up as the npm package, so it gets the same version in the same branch (mcr.microsoft.com has no release timestamps, the npm registry does). If the image for a new version is not pushed yet, test:pw:update:linux fails to pull it until it is.

packageRules.description: Majors are planned work, not a weekly chore.

Test-only dependencies such as serve: one pull request for their minor and patch updates. Playwright has a rule of its own below, and the rule for what ships takes every other npm dependency back out of this group.

@playwright/test and the Docker image tag from the custom manager in one branch. The explicit group keeps the npm package and both image tags in one branch named renovate/playwright, whatever the presets group. Pinned, so that nobody re-adds a ^ and lock file maintenance cannot move it away from the image tag. Test-only, so no approval.
prBodyNotes: Screenshots can change with the browser. If the visual tests fail, regenerate both baseline sets (`npm run test:pw:update` on macOS and `npm run test:pw:update:linux`, see test/README.md) and review the diff.

Commit the regenerated baselines with a `test:` commit message, never `fix:` or `feat:`. With a merge commit or a rebase merge every commit on this branch reaches `main` (a squash merge copies their messages into its body), and release-please reads them all.

packageRules.description: Every npm dependency can change what ships (dist/ and dist-npm/), whatever its type: dependencies, peerDependencies, or a build tool or plugin in devDependencies. The exceptions are the test-only packages negated in matchPackageNames, which this rule leaves to the rules above. A new test-only package has to be added to that exemption list to become routine. Every update waits for a tick and gets a pull request of its own (the null group takes it back out of the dev dependencies group).
prBodyNotes: **Changes what ships.** Run `npm run build` and `npm run build:npm` on `main` and on this branch and diff `dist/` and `dist-npm/`. Check that the syntax target of the output has not moved (neither vite config sets `build.target`, so it follows the vite default). A security fix opens here without the approval step.

packageRules.description: Build tools and plugins in devDependencies are pinned to exact versions, so that lock file maintenance cannot move them inside a range without a tick. A newly added one with a ^ range first gets a pin pull request, itself behind a tick; its updates follow once that is merged, so tick the pin (or add the package with an exact version). Only devDependencies: a range in dependencies or peerDependencies is what consumers of the package resolve against, and pinning it is a decision for whoever adds one.
One pull request for the CI plumbing: the actions in .github/workflows. release-please-action and the Renovate image have groups of their own below.

release-please-action out of the GitHub Actions group, into a pull request of its own: it bundles the release-please engine, which decides when and what this repository releases. After the GitHub Actions rule, so that this group wins. Majors stay behind the majors rule.
prBodyNotes: **Decides releases.** This action bundles the release-please engine, which decides when and what this repository releases. Read its release notes for changes to how commits are parsed and versions are bumped.

packageRules.description: The Renovate image receives the App token, and ghcr.io publishes no release dates: without timestamp-optional the minimum release age would hold every image back for ever, and with it the age is not checked at all. So the image gets a pull request of its own, once a month, with the check left to the person who merges it. No PR limits, for the same reason as lock file maintenance: with a once-a-month window the limits would starve it. After the GitHub Actions rule, so that this group wins.
prBodyNotes: **Runs with the App token.** The registry reports no release date, so the 3-day release age was not applied to this image. Before merging, check on github.com/renovatebot/renovate/releases that this version was published at least 3 days ago, and that the digest in the diff is the one the registry serves for that tag.

If this takes the image to 44.232.0 or later, also change `dependencyDashboardOSVVulnerabilitySummary` in renovate.json to `"dependencyDashboard": { "osvVulnerabilitySummary": "unresolved" }` in this pull request. Renovate migrates the old key in memory either way, but the Dependency Dashboard shows a migration notice until the file is changed.

packageRules.description: Pins and digest updates carry no release timestamp of their own (a pin changes no version; lookup already ages a digest through the version it belongs to). Under the default timestamp-required their renovate/stability-days status would stay pending for ever.
.nvmrc holds a major (24), so only majors are proposed, and the majors rule gates them.
prBodyNotes: `.nvmrc` sets the Node version for both CI and `publish.yml`, so this also changes the runtime that builds and publishes the package to npm.
